questions.key_step: Differentiate g(f(x))=x twice to get g''=-f''/f'^3 and solve f(x)=4.
questions.justification: Standard inverse-derivative formula chained with solving a cubic by inspection; no hidden idea, options allow a check. Same demand as a routine chain of results.

questions.key_step: C1 needs k>2 (x^(k-2)cos(1/x)->0); then optimise V with S=36pi.
questions.justification: Two routine stages: a known threshold for x^k sin(1/x) and a textbook open-cylinder maximisation; no insight beyond practice.
One familiar move (differentials at the inflection point) with trivial arithmetic.

questions.key_step: The functional equation forces f=x^2+x; kinks of max/min occur where branches with different slopes cross.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (solve the functional equation, then analyse three-branch max and min with four options to judge); more demanding than a single max/min question.

questions.key_step: Implicit differentiation of y^3+y=x gives f'=1/(3y^2+1); check one-sided derivatives at 0 and sign of f''.
questions.justification: Four statements, each routine (piecewise differentiability, implicit derivative, concavity); several concepts so the MCQ floor of 2.5 applies.

questions.key_step: C1 and C2 are mirror images in y=x so d1=2*dist(C1,y=x); d2 is a quartic minimisation.
questions.justification: Two distinct minimisation problems with a symmetry insight and four options; moderate chain length.

questions.key_step: Series of ln x/(x-1) near 1 (or repeated L'Hopital) gives all four limits.
questions.justification: Four limit statements each needing a real computation (tangent intercepts, L'Hopital twice); every option must be verified.

questions.key_step: A tangent through the origin needs a(1+ln a)=1 with a unique root; also 0^0 and x^(1/x) maximum.
questions.justification: Four statements with logarithmic differentiation, a monotonicity argument for uniqueness and a double-tangent check.

questions.key_step: Divide f''=-ff'^2 by f' to integrate: f'=e^(-f^2/2); then sign analysis of g' and h'.
questions.justification: One non-routine integration trick then three short sign checks; the trick is learnable.

questions.key_step: f is odd, concave on x>0 and f/x falls from 1 to 0; counting roots of f=cx needs the shape of k(x).
questions.justification: Four statements, one needing a global IVT/roots argument with limits at infinity; heavier than Q9 on the same set-up.

questions.key_step: f is strictly increasing on [-2,-1], so a root lies inside iff f(-2)f(-1)<0; endpoints excluded.
questions.justification: Three routine steps with an endpoint trap on an integer answer.

questions.key_step: Expand to y-x-y^2cos x+xy^2 sin x=0 and differentiate twice at (0,1).
questions.justification: Long exact computation twice differentiated; one slip changes the answer and there are no options.

questions.key_step: Match slope and intercept of common tangents and count real roots of 9s^4-8s^3-18s^2+13 by monotonicity.
questions.justification: Chain of several stages with precision risk in counting the roots of a quartic via critical values; no options.

questions.key_step: Hermite's identity gives f=[2x]; the limit selects x+2 for |x|<1 and [2x] for |x|>1; check x=+-1 and jump points.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas plus careful discontinuity counting at switch points and jumps; one slip changes the count.

questions.key_step: MVT gives c=2; orthogonality means m1*m2=-1.
questions.justification: Routine chain of three standard results; the numerical format adds no check.

questions.key_step: Use logarithmic derivatives: (x/y)dy/dx=(y'/y)/(x'/x) and the expression collapses to t.
questions.justification: Routine logarithmic differentiation with an algebraic cancellation.

questions.key_step: Take e^x,e^2x,e^3x out of the columns; y=2u^6 in u=e^x.
questions.justification: Two routine steps (determinant simplification, differentiate a power) with a small idea of changing variable to u.
